# Radar view — design

* Date: 2026-09-25
* Requirements: FR‑1.15 (new), FR‑1.9, FR‑1.11, FR‑1.12, FR‑1.13, FR‑1.14, QS‑2.3, QS‑4.4
* Prototype: `docs/concepts/radar-prototype.svg` (generated by `docs/concepts/radar-prototype.py`)

## 1. What it is

A fourth view, `GET /radar`, drawing every open item of the snapshot as a blip on an air-traffic
radar scope. It answers the product's one question — *does anything need me right now?* — as a
picture: what is close to the centre moved recently, what glows needs the owner, what wears hazard
tape is a security or dependency item.

## 2. Encoding

| Channel | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Bearing (sector) | The site claiming the item's repository, one equal sector per entry of `siteSpecs` (configured sites in order, then Other). An item whose repository no spec names — left over from an earlier configuration — goes to Other, which is then drawn even when every configured repository is claimed. |
| Position inside the sector | Deterministic: CRC‑32 of `repo#number`, spread over the sector minus a 4° margin on each side. The same item stands in the same place on every render. |
| Distance from centre | Time since `UpdatedAt`, log scale: `r = r0 + (R − r0 − 10) · ln(1 + days) / ln(1 + 730)`, clamped to the rim. Unknown `UpdatedAt` sits on the rim. Range rings at 1 d, 1 wk, 1 mo, 6 mo, 1 yr. |
| Shape | Circle = issue, diamond = pull request. |
| Fill | The site's colour (`hue-*` classes, lightened in dark as the tiles do). |
| Security (Tier security, FR‑1.13) | Larger mark, red hazard-tape ring, fast red pulse, red `⚠ #n` tag. Never fades. |
| Dependency (Tier dependency) | Amber hazard-tape ring. Never fades. |
| Needs you (`domain.NeedsNow`, reason review or contribution) | Accent-blue ring with a slow pulse, blue `#n` tag. |
| Age fade | Four fade buckets by the item's ring (≤1 wk, ≤1 mo, ≤6 mo, older). |

Colour is never the only signal: the shapes, the tape rings, the tags and the data block say it in
words.

## 3. Interaction

* Every blip is an `<a href="{item URL}" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` — clicking
  opens the item on GitHub in a new tab, as everywhere else.
* Hovering or focusing a blip shows its **data block** in the panel beside the scope: kind,
  repository, number, title (wrapped), the reason it is loud, author, opened, last activity,
  labels, the first two lines of its summary, and "opens on GitHub ↗". A dotted leader joins blip
  and panel. With nothing hovered, the panel holds the legend and the counts.
* All of it is CSS (`:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:has`) in `app.css`; no JavaScript.
* The `aria-label` of each blip names kind, repository, number, title and its mark.

## 4. Motion

A sweep beam with an afterglow rotates once every 8 s. Each blip flashes as the beam passes: its
animation delay is its bearing, rounded to one of 36 classes `bearing-0 … bearing-35` defined in
`app.css` — never a `style` attribute, which the CSP (no `'unsafe-inline'`) would refuse. Under
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` nothing moves.

## 5. Placement in the product

* The switch becomes List | Sites | Radar | Contributors.
* The cogwheel's "Open at" offers Radar; the landing cookie accepts `radar`, which redirects
  `GET /` to `/radar` like the other views.
* `/radar` is an `authSessionPage` route and goes through `answeredWaiting` like every page
  (FR‑1.9).
* The page carries the shared header (fetched time, error notice).

## 6. Rendering

Server-rendered inline SVG, `viewBox="0 0 1560 1000"`, scope on the left, panel on the right. Go
computes every coordinate and every wrapped line (`internal/web/radar.go`); the template
(`templates/radar.html`) only prints. Colours are CSS custom properties with `light-dark()`, so the
appearance switch applies. On a narrow screen the SVG scales to the width; tapping a blip opens the
item.

## 7. Budget

QS‑2.3's 150 kB over the representative fixture (150 items) is a test, as for the other views. Card
text uses one `<text>` with `<tspan dy>` lines to keep each blip small.

## 8. Out of scope

Pinning a data block (a click now opens GitHub), clustering of crowded sectors, moving blips, a
second layout for phones.
